name: TLE5012BE1000
title: TLE5012B: GMR 360° magnetic angle sensor with SSC, PWM, IIF, HSM and SPC interfaces, PG-DSO-8
summary: A magnetic angle sensor built on integrated giant magnetoresistance bridges that measure the sine and cosine of an in-plane field and turn them into a 0° to 360° angle with 15-bit resolution, plus revolution count and angular speed. Over life and temperature the angle error is at most 1.0° with autocalibration on. A three-wire SPI-compatible SSC port up to 8 Mbit/s configures and reads it, and one secondary interface (incremental quadrature, Hall switch emulation, PWM or SAE J2716-based SPC) can run beside SSC or alone. Five preset derivatives (E1000 IIF, E3005 HSM, E5000 and E5020 PWM, E9000 SPC) differ only in start-up configuration. It runs from 3.0 V to 5.5 V, is AEC-Q100 qualified for -40 °C to 150 °C junction, and comes in PG-DSO-8.

circuits.title: IIF interface and SSC (IIF in push-pull configuration)
circuits.description: The E1000 wiring: the three interface pins drive a controller's quadrature-counter inputs directly as push-pull outputs (phase A, phase B, index), while SSC stays connected for configuration and for reading the absolute angle. 100 Ω in series with CSQ and SCK guards against noise, and 470 Ω in DATA limits the current if sensor and controller ever drive the line against each other. A 100 nF capacitor decouples VDD. If IFA, IFB and IFC are set to open-drain instead, each needs a pull-up to VDD, for example 2.2 kΩ.

circuits.title: HSM interface and SSC (HSM in push-pull configuration)
circuits.description: The E3005 wiring: IFA, IFB and IFC stand in for three Hall switches (HS1 to HS3) of a motor commutation input, driven push-pull, with SSC alongside. Series resistors on the SSC lines (100 Ω on CSQ and SCK, 470 Ω on DATA) and a 100 nF VDD capacitor as in the IIF circuit.

circuits.title: HSM interface and SSC (HSM in open-drain configuration)
circuits.description: Hall switch emulation with the three interface pins set to open-drain over SSC, so each Hall line gets a 2.2 kΩ pull-up to VDD. The SSC side keeps its 100 Ω and 470 Ω series resistors and VDD its 100 nF capacitor.

circuits.title: PWM interface (push-pull configuration)
circuits.description: The E5000 wiring, PWM only: the angle leaves on IFA as a push-pull PWM signal. CSQ is tied to VDD so the SSC interface stays deselected, SCK, IFB and IFC go to ground, and DATA is left open; CSQ and DATA have internal pull-ups. VDD is decoupled with 100 nF.

circuits.title: PWM interface (open-drain configuration)
circuits.description: The E5020 wiring: PWM on IFA as an open-drain output with a 2.2 kΩ pull-up to VDD. CSQ is tied to VDD to hold SSC inactive, SCK, IFB and IFC are grounded and DATA is open; 100 nF decouples VDD.

circuits.title: SPC interface
circuits.description: The E9000 wiring: SPC on IFA, open-drain, with a 2.2 kΩ pull-up to VDD; the same line carries the controller's trigger pulse in. IFC and SCK at ground set slave number 00. To give SCK a high level for another slave number, CSQ must go to ground instead, so SSC is not used alongside SPC. CSQ to VDD, IFB to ground, DATA open, and 100 nF on VDD.

circuits.title: SSC interface with push-pull configuration (high-speed application)
circuits.description: The SSC link between the sensor and a controller's SPI-type port, DATA in its default push-pull mode. The controller's MTSR and MRST pins are joined and reach DATA through 470 Ω, which limits the current if the sensor drives high while the controller drives low or the other way round. CSQ and SCK come from the controller through 100 Ω each, against noise and disturbances.

circuits.title: SSC interface with open-drain configuration (bus systems)
circuits.description: DATA set to open-drain (bit SSC_OD) so several SSC slaves, for example two sensors for redundancy, can share one controller line. A 1 kΩ pull-up to VDD holds the shared data node, with 100 Ω in series on each side of it: one to the sensor's DATA, one to the controller's joined MTSR and MRST. CSQ and SCK each pass through 100 Ω. Each sensor is addressed by its own CSQ, so a push-pull bus also works.

circuits.title: Sensors' supply in bus mode
circuits.description: Two or more sensors share one SPC line into a controller's capture-compare input, with a single pull-up on the line. Every sensor runs from the same VDD as the others: a sensor that loses its supply sinks current from the shared output line and can upset the bus. Each sensor and the controller has its own VDD capacitor.
notes: Each sensor's OUT pin is its SPC output, IFA.

equations.name: SSC CRC
equations.note: SAE J1850 CRC over every byte of a transfer, commands included, computed with a fast parallel CRC circuit; it restarts with each transfer and the remainder is sent inverted.

equations.name: SPC CRC nibble
equations.note: Computed over the status nibble together with all data nibbles; what remains once the final data nibble is processed is transmitted.

operation.text: Giant magnetoresistive elements sit on top of the CMOS logic. Two full bridges of four elements each respond to the in-plane field: one gives the X (cosine) signal, the other the Y (sine) signal. Each element has a pinned reference direction; resistance is lowest when the outside field is parallel to it and highest when anti-parallel. One bridge alone repeats every 180°, so the two orthogonal bridges together, combined by ARCTAN2, give a true 0° to 360° angle. The full-bridge layout gives the largest signal and lets temperature effects cancel.
Placement of the die in the package can rotate the sensor's 0° direction by up to 3° from the package edge.

Three regulators fed straight from VDD supply the GMR bridges (VRG), the analogue section (VRA) and the logic (VRD, taken from VRA). Sigma-delta converters turn the X, Y and temperature signals into numbers. The digital processing unit holds a state machine that corrects offset, offset drift, amplitude mismatch and non-orthogonality and runs autocalibration, prediction and speed calculation; a CORDIC that computes the angle; a capture-compare unit that makes the PWM and SPC waveforms; RAM holding the configuration registers; and laser fuses holding the calibration and default configuration, copied into RAM at start-up. The angle is given with 15 bits (0.01°) and sine and cosine with 16 bits; the part also counts revolutions and measures angular speed.

A PLL makes the digital clock, normally from the internal oscillator. Set over SSC, the PLL can instead lock to an external clock on IFC to synchronise the sensor with other chips; this works only with the PWM or SPC interface. The PLL triggers on rising edges and needs the pulse widths of the external clock table, with a duty cycle of 30 % to 70 % (50 % typical). If more than two edges go missing, the chip resets itself and restarts on its internal clock, flagged by S_RST, CLK_SEL and the safety word. All timings move with the clock spread.

Once VDD is above its minimum the part is ready after the power-on time of 5 ms typical, 7 ms maximum; built-in self-tests of the state machine, CORDIC, CCU and ADCs run during start-up. Register writes are refused until then, except the switch to the external clock, which is confirmed by reading it back. A fast reset (0.5 ms max) is done by turning off the start-up self-test (S_BIST = 0) and then setting AS_RST = 1.

SSC is a three-wire, SPI-compatible, bidirectional link up to 8 Mbit/s for configuration and data. One secondary interface on IFA, IFB and IFC runs alongside it: PWM, incremental (IIF), Hall switch mode (HSM) or short PWM code (SPC). With a preset derivative the secondary interface can be used on its own without SSC. Bit IFAB_OD (register IFAB, 0DH) selects push-pull or open-drain for IFA, IFB and IFC; bit SSC_OD (register MOD_3, 09H) does the same for DATA, which is push-pull by default. Pin drive strength and slope are set in MOD_3.

The magnet's field, stated at TJ = 25 °C, must fall inside the allowed band, which narrows as the highest junction temperature rises. Every upper limit starts at 100 mT at -40 °C; for TJ up to 85 °C it is 70 mT at 25 °C and 65 mT at 85 °C; for TJ up to 100 °C, 60 mT at 25 °C and 54 mT at 100 °C; for TJ up to 150 °C, 50 mT at 25 °C and 42 mT at 150 °C. The lower limit is 30 mT at 25 °C. Below it, down to 25 mT, the sensor works with 0.1° more angle error at 0 h. A stronger field than the band allows is possible at higher temperatures if extra angle error is accepted.

The overall angle error is relative: the deviation from a straight reference line once a zero angle is defined, for a static field. A rotating field adds a speed-dependent error from the angle delay time; prediction reduces it in fast-turning use. With autocalibration on, a temperature change of more than 5 K within 1.5 revolutions adds the error of the additional angle error curve, which depends on the change and on the starting temperature; the curves are the worst case, a rise, and a fall gives less. Once the temperature settles and 1.5 revolutions pass, the error is back to the table figure.

Autocalibration recalculates the compensation parameters while running, lowering the drift error from temperature and ageing. It needs 1.5 revolutions to form new parameters, keeps updating them, and moves them by one LSB at a time so the output never jumps. AUTOCAL in MOD_2 selects: 00 off; 01 mode 1, one LSB per update time tupd (set by FIR_MD) until the new values are reached; 10 mode 2, one LSB per full 1.5-revolution parameter generation, then a new calculation; 11 mode 3, one LSB per 11.25° of angle until the new values are reached. It is on by default only in some derivatives.

The angle reaches the output after the converter, filter and calculation delay, which depends on the filter (FIR_MD) and the interface. Prediction adds the difference between the latest angle and the two before it, estimating where the field will be after the delay.

Transfers are word-aligned 16-bit words, MSB first. The master opens with a command word (RW, lock, UPD, address, number of data words), then data words follow, then the sensor appends a safety word with status bits, its sensor-number response and an 8-bit CRC. With ND = 0 one register is read and no safety word is sent, for the fastest readout. With ND > 1 consecutive registers are read, wrapping from 3FH to 00H. Data changes on the rising edge of SCK and is sampled on the falling edge. After changing data direction the master waits twr_delay. Raising CSQ aborts a transfer at once and resets the CRC. A transfer ends after the safety word, and CSQ must then stay high for at least tCSoff. In push-pull mode the DATA driver is on only while the sensor sends; otherwise DATA is high impedance.

Pulsing CSQ low and back high without any SCK clock copies all registers that have an update buffer, at one instant, into those buffers. A read with UPD = 1 then returns that consistent snapshot instead of live values. Such bits are marked u in the register types.

Selected with IF_MD = 01. The duty cycle follows the last measured angle (AVAL) with 12-bit resolution at about 0.25, 0.5, 1 or 2 kHz, chosen in IFAB_RES. Duty cycles of 6.25 % to 93.75 % carry the angle; 0 % to 6.25 % and 93.75 % to 100 % are kept for diagnosis. An error sets its status bit and moves the output into the low band (electrical errors, about 2 %) or the high band (system errors, about 98 %). The output shows an error while it lasts and at least once; the status register keeps it until read over SSC or a reset. An S_ADCT error is shown until the next reset. This diagnostic output can be turned off in MOD_4.

SPC follows SAE J2716 SENT nibble coding but sends a frame only when the controller triggers it with a low pulse on IFA, so up to four sensors can share one line. The trigger's low time selects the sensor; its slave number comes from the levels on SCK (S_NR[0]) and IFC (S_NR[1]). A frame is: trigger, a 56-unit synchronisation period (during which a new sample is taken), a status nibble, three to six data nibbles, a CRC nibble and an end pulse. Each nibble is a 3-unit low pulse followed by a high time, 12 to 27 units in all for values 0 to 15. The full frame carries a 16-bit angle and an 8-bit temperature. In SPC mode the angle is calculated only on a trigger, and AVAL holds the angle from the last trigger. The sensor accepts the next trigger 90 µs after the end pulse falls. A trigger whose low time is longer than the maximum gets no answer, and the sensor is ready again 30 µs after the pulse crosses Vth. The status nibble flags errors as the PWM bands do, with the same holding rules and the same MOD_4 switch. The unit time is 3 µs, trimmable to 2.5, 2.0 or 1.5 µs in IFAB_HYST.

Selected with IF_MD = 010. IFA, IFB and IFC emulate three Hall switches for motor commutation: each output is high for 180° electrical, the three are 120° electrical apart, and an edge comes every 60° electrical; the pole-pair count is set in HSM_PLP (register 0EH), and mechanical 0° is always the reference. Output is normally push-pull and can be set to open-drain in IFAB_OD. A switching hysteresis keeps rotor vibration from toggling the outputs.

IIF behaves like an optical quadrature encoder with 50 % duty: one pulse per angle step, 9 to 12 bits per turn (512 to 4096 steps) set in IFAB_RES. In A/B mode the phase order of IFA and IFB gives the direction (A after B is clockwise); in step/direction mode IFA pulses the steps and IFB's level gives the direction; IIF_MOD in MOD_1 chooses. The controller needs an up/down counter; it can compare the counter with AVAL read over SSC and add any difference. After start-up the sensor sends as many pulses as the absolute angle, so the counter starts at the true position. IFC gives an index pulse at 0°. Fewer bits do not raise the highest rotation speed.

For a self-check, ADCTV_EN in the SIL register switches the converter inputs from the bridges to a resistor divider, and ADCTV_X and ADCTV_Y pick fixed X and Y values that stand for magnet positions; the angle in AVAL then shows whether the converters work. Available sets: 4 points on a 70 % circle (0°, 90°, 180°, 270°); 8 points on a 100 % circle (every 45°); 8 points on a 122.1 % circle (35.3°, 54.7°, 125.3°, 144.7°, 215.3°, 234.7°, 305.3°, 324.7°); 4 points on a 141.4 % circle (45°, 135°, 225°, 315°).

Comparators watch the internal supplies. A fault must last at least 256 digital clock periods to set its status bit, which filters spikes. Over- and undervoltage set S_VR, shown in the SSC safety word, the SPC status nibble or the PWM low diagnostic band. Each 2.5 V regulator has an overvoltage comparator; a separate one watches VDD itself. The GND-off comparator compares GND with SCK and detects a lost ground connection. The VDD-off comparator detects a lost VDD connection, in which case the chip is fed from SCK and CSQ through their ESD structures.

The part supports SIL-oriented designs with: converter test vectors and inversion or combination of the filter input streams (both set over SSC), an 8-bit CRC on SSC and a 4-bit CRC on SPC, start-up self-tests, two interfaces active at once, and over- and undervoltage detection.
With two or more sensors on one SSC or SPC bus, all of them should share one supply, because an unpowered sensor sinks current through its output and may disturb the bus.
When SSC is not used, CSQ is tied to VDD for a firm high level so the interface is never selected by accident, and DATA is left open; both have internal pull-ups.

The centre of the sensitive area lies on the package centrelines within 0.4 mm, inside a 0.644 mm circle, 1.22 ± 0.18 mm above the seating plane and at least 0.32 mm below the top of the body. The die tilts by 3° at most relative to the seating plane.
